2071.note: Not assessed, and probably read. Ribier II (archive.org bub_gb_qWTswSr32NYC, djvu text, re-read 16 Nov) pp. 768-769 prints a letter from 'Le Roy' to 'M. l'Evesq. d'Angoulesme, Ambassadeur à Rome', dated only '14. Aoust' (1558, with no place). It runs about 1.3 printed pages on the Caraffa nephews: keep them hopeful with fair words and decide nothing before the battle with Philip II. The Morgan letter is dated 13 Aug and is 5 1/4 pp., 'much of which is in cipher'. The Morgan leaf, which would settle whether this is the same letter, is still behind Cloudflare (themorgan.org 403 to curl and WebFetch; no Wayback copy of literary-historical/103825).

2116.note: Not assessed: the edition blocker stands, and a new piece of literature points to contemporary solution. The 4 Nov Chrome pass already saw the cipher (Benson StoryMap) and counted the TARO items (about 54 'In code', 88 'Partly in code', 5 'with a translation'; key sheets in the archive). This pass found Smoot, Parker Hitt: The Father of American Military Cryptology (2022), which says intercepted messages of Lazaro de la Garza, Villa's agent at Ciudad Juarez, came to Hitt's code-breaking effort (Google Books feed snippet, id y90uEAAAQBAJ). Osorio's La correspondencia de Francisco Villa (1986/1988, 2004/2006 eds.) is still unopened. Whether the US Army or Osorio left readings of these particular items is open.
2116.access_note: Benson Latin American Collection reading room. TARO guide txarchives.org/utlac/finding_aids/00075.xml answers. Osorio and Smoot are in-copyright books: only Google Books snippets are reachable.

2119.note: Not assessed, and probably printed. Google Books feed snippets of Akkerman, Correspondence of Elizabeth Stuart II (2011; id CA1T_SaqiicC) show that the edition prints a Morgan letter: 'Signed secretarial original in the hand of Theobald Maurice, Pierpont Morgan Library, New York, Rulers of England James I / 161689 - MA Unassigned, no. 107a. Address: A Monsieur de Rustorf a Hamburg'. Morgan record 161689 sits next to this lead's record 161690 (The Hague, 6 Feb 1635, 'Partly in cipher'), so Akkerman used this Morgan group. Since she deciphers Elizabeth's cipher letters, the 6 Feb 1635 letter is very likely printed deciphered, but no snippet tied a letter number to 161690.
2119.access_note: Morgan reading room (themorgan.org/literary-historical/161690, 403 to scripts). Akkerman vol. II page view in Chrome: https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/CA1T_SaqiicC?gbpv=1&bsq=161690 (or bsq=MA Unassigned).

2198.note: Not assessed: the blocker stands, and prior art looks more likely. Google Books feed snippets show that Concilium Tridentinum X (Buschbell 1916) prints letters of Giovanni Battista Cervini to Cardinal Cervini from the Carte Cerviniane originals ('C. Cerv.'): a letter of 24 Apr 1546 at pp. 891-892, cited in Das Bildnis der Geliebten (2007), and an index entry 'Cervini litterae' at p. 953. These fall inside the APUG 690rec register's span (11 Apr 1546-30 Aug 1547). Whether the 17th-c. register holds code groups or deciphered copies, and whether CT X prints the cipher passages, is still unseen.

2491.note: Not assessed. The holder in the lead record is wrong: the GAK inventory page (fetched 16 Nov, HTTP 200) names the holder of Ar. Eis. 176 as the Benaki Museum, Historical Archives Department (Μουσείο Μπενάκη, Τμήμα Ιστορικών Αρχείων), not GAK Central Service. The fonds is 287 documents and 71 photographs, 1891-1939, given by Natalia Mela. The description is taken from Tselika, Guide to the Historical Archives of the Benaki Museum (2006). Natalia Mela drew on these same papers for her 1926 book Pavlos Melas, which prints letters by him and others, so a printed or deciphered text of the 1904 cipher letters is likely and was not checked.
